narration.speaker: god
narration.text: The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them.
Those words were spoken over the whole world. Every man, every woman, every child. How did it come to this, and would anyone be left?
Ten generations after Eden, the earth is full of people, and full of noise. Cities of tents cover the plains, and nobody looks up.
And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
Not some thoughts. Every one. Only evil. Continually. And it did not stay inside their hearts for long.
Men bow down to what their own hands have carved. Brothers turn on brothers. The strong take what they want, and the weak learn to hide.
The earth also was corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with violence.
Violence in every camp, and on every road. At the wells, in the markets, in the tents at night. And then comes a line most readers rush past.
And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
The text does not say God was angry first. It says He was grieved, at His heart. The Maker of the world, hurting over what His people became.
And God looked upon the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.
The word corrupt comes three times in two verses. The writer wants you to feel the weight of it.
He looked, and all of it had turned. Not one city. Not one family. All flesh. And then He spoke.

narration.speaker: god
narration.text: I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth;
Not man alone. The beasts of the field, the creeping things, the birds of the air. Everything that breathes on the land.

narration.speaker: god
narration.text: For it repenteth me that I have made them.
It sounds like the end of the story. But in the middle of all that violence, one small word changes everything.
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
One man and his family, walking the other way, while the whole world ran past them.
Notice the order. Grief comes before judgment. The flood is not the story of a cold God, but of a wounded heart.
Would you have kept walking against the crowd? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part eight tomorrow: Noah builds the ark.
